items.origin: The Alexander legends told in later storytelling
items.claim: Dhul-Qarnayn was Alexander the Great, who travelled to the ends of the earth, reached the place where the sun sets, and walled in Gog and Magog.
items.ruling: Not told here. Ibn Kathir (abridged) calls the storytellers’ accounts of the sun’s setting-place myths of the People of the Book, and Ma’ariful Qur’an, following Ibn Kathir, rejects the identification with Alexander of Macedon because Alexander was a polytheist, while noting that Abu Hayyan and al-Alusi held it. The Qur’an itself names no such person.
items.basis: Tafsir Ibn Kathir (abridged English edition, read on Quran.com), on 18:85-88; Ma’ariful Qur’an (English edition, read on Quran.com), on 18:83

items.origin: A modern scholarly identification, reported in Ma’ariful Qur’an
items.claim: Dhul-Qarnayn was Cyrus the Great of Persia, who freed the Israelites from Babylon.
items.ruling: The Qur’an does not name him. Ma’ariful Qur’an reports this as the research of Hifzur-Rahman in Qasas al-Qur’an and says it does not decide between the views. We neither believe nor disbelieve it, and the story here tells only what the verses say.
items.basis: Ma’ariful Qur’an (English edition, read on Quran.com), on 18:83
